We have a target molecule: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions. The guidance: steps enumerated in order they must be applied (forward). So retrosynthesis steps are reverse of forward. The hints: 1) Carboxylic acid to amide via coupling agent (C-O broken, C-N formed). That's amide formation step. 2) Doebner Modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (new alkene). So that creates the C=C double bond and carboxylic acid. 3) Sulfonamide formation: amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide.

Thus the target has a sulfonamide linking a tolyl sulfonyl group to a phenyl ring (the sulfonyl attached to aromatic ring). Also an amide linking the unsaturated chain to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So we can plan retrosynthesis:

Target T: p-tolyl-sulfonyl-phenyl-alkenyl-amide-aniline (with an extra NH on aniline). Actually structure: tolyl (CH3 on phenyl) attached to sulfonamide N (NSO2) attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). That phenyl has para substituent: /C=C/C(=O)N-aryl (aniline). So we can break at sulfonamide formation: disconnection between sulfonyl chloride and amine. So precursor 1: p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (CH3-Ph-SO2Cl) and amine precursor: the rest of molecule (the phenyl with unsaturated amide and aniline). Actually sulfonamide formed from sulfonyl chloride + amine (the nitrogen attached to sulfonyl). In target, the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the tolyl sulfonyl group and to the phenyl ring (the N is attached to phenyl). So the amine precursor would be the phenyl ring bearing the N (aniline) that is attached to sulfonyl group. So we need the amine: H2N-Ph- (the phenyl that later gets sulfonyl). That phenyl also has the unsaturated amide substituent at para position. So precursor A: aniline with para substituent of α,β-unsaturated amide (C=C-C(=O)NH-Ph-NH2?). Wait the amide attaches to aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). Actually the amide is C(=O)N attached to an aniline (c3ccccc3N). So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl (aniline) which has an NH2 group (para?). The SMILES: ...C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N. So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl that has an NH2 substituent (aniline). So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl ring (c3ccccc3N). So the amide nitrogen is part of the chain: ...C(=O)N-Ph-NH2. So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl which also has an NH2 (maybe at para). So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl at position 1, and the phenyl has an NH2 at position? The SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N means an aniline with two nitrogens? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" is an aniline where the nitrogen is attached to the aromatic carbon (the first N is attached to carbonyl, then aromatic carbon, then the ring has another N substituent at the end (the last N). So it's a 1,4-diaminobenzene? The pattern: N-Ph-N (para). So the amide attaches to a phenyl that also has an NH2 para to the amide.

Thus the amide formation step: we can disconnect the amide bond between carbonyl carbon and the amide nitrogen (attached to phenyl). So precursor: α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (the chain) and an aniline (c3ccccc3N). So step 2: Doebner modification to create the α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid from aromatic aldehyde and malonic acid. The aldehyde would be the phenyl ring (the one attached to sulfonamide) with aldehyde at para position (where the chain attaches). So precursor: aromatic aldehyde (p-formyl phenyl attached to sulfonamide) and malonic acid to give the unsaturated acid. Then step 1: sulfonamide formation from sulfonyl chloride and amine (the phenyl with aldehyde). So overall three steps.

Thus we need to produce a JSON route: root molecule target, then reaction nodes with template IDs. We need to find appropriate template IDs for each transformation. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria to find templates for sulfonamide formation, amide formation, Doebner modification (which is a Knoevenagel condensation with malonic acid? Actually Doebner modification forms α,β-unsaturated acid from aldehyde + malonic acid. So functional groups broken: aldehyde, carboxylic acid (malonic) maybe? Formed: C-C double bond, carboxylic acid (the product). So we can search.
